name: Erect, operate and dismantle cranes
summary: The equipment team plans each tower crane erection, climb and dismantle and each mobile crane set-up for a heavy or critical lift. The equipment manager assesses the site, an outside engineer designs bases and reviews critical plans, the superintendent gets street permits and prepares the site, certified operators set up and run the crane with a signaller, and an engineer inspects tower cranes before use. Municipal permits, engineer availability and wind decide the day, and a postponed lift means rebooking the assist crane, trucks and traffic control.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor of about 2,800 people that owns about 12 tower cranes and 6 mobile cranes and rents larger cranes with operators.
baseline.notes: One case is one crane event; day-to-day tower crane operation during pours is part of concrete placement.

unit_of_work: one crane set-up, critical lift or dismantle
trigger: A project asks the equipment team for a tower crane erection, climb or dismantle, or a mobile crane for a heavy or critical lift.
end_state: The crane has been set up and the lift made, or the tower crane erected, inspected and put in service, or dismantled and removed; logs are recorded and the lift plan filed and sent to the site.

volume.seasonality: More erections in spring and dismantles in late fall; winter lifts lose days to wind and cold.

evidence.note: Org file estimate: about 15% tower erections, 10% climbs, 15% dismantles, 60% mobile crane set-ups and critical lifts.

surge.cause: construction season (May to October), when structures go up and cranes are erected

evidence.note: Estimate in line with the org file's construction season surge.
Three equipment and yard managers in the org file; crane planning is a large part of one manager's job across regions; estimate.
Permits, site preparation and pre-lift meetings; estimate.
Set-ups, erections, climbs, dismantles and critical lifts only; daily tower crane operation for pours sits in concrete placement. Estimate.
Assembly checks and repairs; not listed in the process map roles.
Signallers; not listed in the process map roles.
Bookings of assist cranes and trucks; not listed in the process map roles.

systems.name: Equipment management (fleet register, rates, maintenance work orders)
Project management platform (drawings, RFIs, submittals, daily logs, change events)
Safety management system (hazard assessments, inspections, incidents, training records)

resources.name: Pickup trucks for superintendents, foremen and safety staff

steps.name: Receive the crane request
steps.description: The equipment and yard manager receives a request from a project for a tower crane erection, climb or dismantle, or for a mobile crane set-up for a heavy or critical lift, with the load, radius, date and site drawings.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Check crane fleet and operator availability
steps.description: The manager checks the register for a free company tower or mobile crane of the right capacity and for certified operators, and decides whether to use company equipment or rent a crane with operator.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Drive to the site
steps.description: The manager drives to the project, usually within a day or two of the request, to see the crane location, access roads, neighbouring buildings and surroundings for himself.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Assess crane location, ground and overhead hazards
steps.description: With the superintendent the manager checks ground bearing and buried services at the outrigger or base location, overhead power lines and their clearances, swing over neighbours and streets, and delivery access for crane components.

error.defect_description: Buried service or ground weakness missed.

control.basis: O. Reg. 213/91 s. 188: minimum distances from energized overhead lines and written measures to prevent encroachment

next.condition: climb, dismantle or mobile crane lift

steps.name: Engineer designs the tower crane base and ties
steps.description: A structural engineer engaged by the company designs the crane foundation or mat, anchor bolts and any building ties from the crane manufacturer's loads and the geotechnical report.

control.basis: Tower crane foundation designed by an engineer to the manufacturer's specifications (O. Reg. 213/91 tower crane provisions)

evidence.note: Requirement for an engineered base is common practice and in Ontario regulation; the section text was not opened. Duration is an estimate.

steps.name: Build the crane base and prepare the site
steps.description: The superintendent schedules excavation, the base pour by the concrete crew and the anchor installation, and keeps the base area clear until the concrete reaches strength.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Prepare the lift or erection plan
steps.description: The manager works out the crane configuration, counterweight, outrigger loads, rigging and the load chart capacity at the working radius, and writes the lift plan or the erection, climbing or dismantling sequence from the manufacturer's manual.

error.defect_description: Capacity, rigging weight or radius miscalculated.

next.condition: critical lift or tower crane work

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Engineer reviews the plan
steps.description: For critical lifts (near capacity, tandem or over occupied areas) and for tower crane erection, climbing and dismantling, an engineer reviews the plan, the climbing system and ties and stamps it or asks for changes.

control.basis: Company critical lift procedure and O. Reg. 213/91 s. 159: engineer inspection of tower crane climbing systems before the first climb

evidence.note: s. 159 covers climbing; the critical-lift review is company practice (tier C).

steps.name: Decide whether a street permit is needed
steps.description: The superintendent checks whether the crane, its outriggers, the assist crane or the boom swing will occupy or pass over the street or sidewalk, which needs a municipal permit and possibly a lane closure.

next.condition: street occupation or swing permit needed

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Apply for the street occupation and hoisting permit
steps.description: The superintendent prepares the application with the lift plan, crane drawings, insurance certificate, traffic control plan and, for tower crane swing, aviation approvals, and files it with the municipality.

error.defect_description: Application missing a drawing or approval.

evidence.note: Toronto's list of requirements; other municipalities ask for less.

steps.name: Municipality reviews and issues the permit
steps.description: The municipality's right-of-way office reviews the application and issues the permit with the allowed dates and hours. Tower crane swing permits in Toronto take about 12 weeks; one-day mobile crane hoisting permits take days to a few weeks.

control.basis: Municipal right-of-way by-laws: street occupation permit for crane hoisting, boom swing and lane closures

evidence.note: Toronto states about 12 weeks for crane applications; the mode is set lower because most permits are for one-day mobile crane hoisting.

steps.name: Book the assist crane, trucks and rentals
steps.description: The yard coordinator books the assist or rental crane with operator, trucks for crane components and counterweights, mats and traffic control for the agreed date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Assign a certified operator
steps.description: The manager assigns an operator and checks the certificate of qualification matches the crane type and capacity, and that the operator knows this crane model.

control.basis: O. Reg. 213/91 s. 150(1): mobile crane operator 1 or 2 or tower crane operator certificate by crane type and capacity; tower crane operator is a compulsory trade

steps.name: Prepare the site for the crane
steps.description: The superintendent clears the crane pad and swing area, sets barricades and traffic control, has utilities covered or de-energized where needed and tells the trades and neighbours about the exclusion zone.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Check the wind forecast and permit window
steps.description: The manager checks the wind forecast against the crane manufacturer's limits for erection and lifting, and the permit's allowed hours, and confirms or postpones the crane, trucks and traffic control the day before.

evidence.note: Postponement share is an estimate; wind limits come from crane manuals.

steps.name: Mobilize the crane to site
steps.description: The operator drives the mobile crane to site, or for tower crane work travels with the crane components, assist crane and counterweight trucks, and checks in at the gate.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Set up, erect, climb or dismantle the crane
steps.description: The operators rig the outriggers and mats and install counterweight, or for tower cranes assemble or dismantle the mast, jib and counter-jib with the assist crane, or jack the crane up a climb. A mobile set-up takes an hour or two; a tower crane erection takes two to three days.

error.defect_description: Bolt, pin or counterweight not installed to the manual.

evidence.note: Operators help set up, dismantle and jack cranes; durations are estimates.

steps.name: Mechanic checks hydraulics and electrics
steps.description: A heavy-duty mechanic connects power, checks hydraulics, limit switches, brakes and load moment indicators and fixes faults found during assembly before the operator takes over.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Operator pre-use inspection and crane log
steps.description: The operator walks the crane before use, checks wire ropes, hooks, limit switches and the load chart on board and records the inspection in the crane log book.

control.basis: O. Reg. 213/91 s. 170: cables inspected by a competent worker at least weekly and recorded in the crane log

steps.name: Engineer inspects the tower crane before use
steps.description: An engineer inspects the erected or climbed tower crane, its base, ties and climbing system, witnesses the load test and issues a written report before the crane goes into service.

control.basis: O. Reg. 213/91 ss. 157(13) and 159: inspection of tower crane shoring, bracing and climbing systems before use

steps.name: Correct erection deficiencies
steps.description: The mechanic and operators fix the deficiencies the engineer noted, such as bolt torque, missing pins or limit switch settings, and call the engineer back.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Hold the pre-lift meeting
steps.description: The superintendent gathers the operator, signaller, riggers and affected trades, goes through the lift plan, exclusion zone, signals and stop-work triggers, and records the hazard assessment.

control.basis: Pre-lift hazard assessment and O. Reg. 213/91 ss. 104 and 106: competent signaller doing no other work when the operator's view is blocked

steps.name: Make the lift or load test
steps.description: The operator makes the critical lift, the tower crane load test or the dismantling picks on the signaller's direction, watching the load moment indicator and wind.

error.defect_description: Load swing or contact with structure.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Signal the lift
steps.description: A trained labourer acts as signaller for the whole lift, in full view of the operator, by radio or hand signals, doing no other work.

steps.name: Rig down and demobilize
steps.description: The operator stows the boom, removes counterweight and mats and drives the mobile crane away; after a tower crane dismantle the components are loaded onto trucks for the yard.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Record hours and defects
steps.description: The operator records crane hours and any defects in the crane log and the equipment system so the project is charged and the shop knows what to fix.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Repair the crane defect
steps.description: The mechanic opens a service work order and repairs or orders parts for the defect; the crane waits in the yard or on site until it is fixed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

steps.name: Distribute the final lift plan and close the job
steps.description: The manager files the lift plan, engineer reports, permits and log entries in the project folder, sends the lift plan to the site and the concrete crews, and closes the crane job.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of common practice for a Canadian union general contractor that self-performs concrete.

exceptions.name: Lift postponed for wind
exceptions.description: The forecast exceeds the crane's wind limit; the crane, trucks and traffic control are rebooked for another day inside the permit window.

exceptions.name: Engineer asks for changes
exceptions.description: The engineer's review of a critical lift or tower crane plan sends it back for a different configuration or rigging.

exceptions.name: Tower crane fails engineer inspection
exceptions.description: The engineer finds erection deficiencies and the crane stays out of service until fixed and re-inspected.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from crane request to job closed
benchmarks.population: Mix of mobile crane lifts and tower crane erections, climbs and dismantles, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: routine mobile lifts within one to three weeks, longer when a street permit is needed (about 45% of cases); tower crane work with engineered bases and swing permits takes two to four months (Toronto states about 12 weeks for crane permit applications).

pain_points.description: Municipal crane swing and street occupation permits take weeks to months and set the earliest date for tower crane work.

evidence.note: About 12 weeks for crane applications in Toronto.

pain_points.description: Wind postpones lifts and erections, and every postponement means rebooking the assist crane, trucks and traffic control.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Outside engineers for bases, critical lift reviews and pre-use inspections are booked days ahead and hold the schedule.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: Rigging | IHSA Construction Safety App
sources.supports: O. Reg. 213/91 crane and hoisting rules: operator certificates by crane type and capacity (s. 150(1)); signaller when the operator's view is blocked, competent and doing no other work (ss. 104, 106); weekly cable inspection recorded in the crane log (s. 170); engineer inspection of tower crane climbing systems before first climb and every 12 months (s. 159); competent-worker inspection of tower crane shoring and bracing before and after each climb and weekly (s. 157(13)); minimum distances and written procedures near energized overhead lines (s. 188).

sources.title: Hoisting Engineer - Tower Crane Operator
sources.supports: Tower crane operation is a compulsory trade in Ontario (certificate of qualification or registered training agreement required); 3,000 hours of training; operators perform pre-operational inspections, plan lifts and calculate capacity, rig, and help set up, dismantle and jack cranes.

sources.title: Street Occupation Permit
sources.supports: Permits needed to occupy the public right of way for mobile crane or boom truck hoisting, tower crane hoisting and boom swing; tower crane swing needs drawings, a $2 million insurance certificate and Transport Canada and Nav Canada approvals; crane applications take about 12 weeks after a complete submission; RoDARS notice required; per-day hoisting and lane closure fees. Page is the 2026 version.

assumptions: One set of triangular ranges covers very different events (a two-hour mobile lift and a three-day tower crane erection), so branch shares carry most of the difference.
Simulated median cycle time (about 18 days) is about 1.2 times the tier C benchmark of 15 days; the permit branch and engineer waits drive the long tail (simulated p90 about 42 days).
The tower-crane resource in the set-up step has a mode of zero because most cases are mobile crane work.
Outside engineers, the municipality and rental crane firms are external waits with no touch time.

The org file's process map sends lift plans to ministry-labour; no rule requiring lift plans to be filed with the regulator in 2019-2022 was found (engineer reports are kept at the project), so that link is left out. Permit applications to the municipality and rental orders to equipment-rental are added.
Mechanics, labourers as signallers and the yard coordinator take part although the process map lists only the equipment manager, crane operators and superintendents.

O. Reg. 213/91 sections are cited from the IHSA summary of the current text; tower crane inspection rules were tightened in 2024-2025, after the reference period, but the cited sections (150, 104, 106, 157, 159, 170, 188) applied in 2019-2022.
The Toronto street occupation page is the 2026 version; 2019-2022 requirements were similar but fees differed.
